patches.value: Fix any δ>0 and apply F003 at the positive scale min(1,δ/sqrt(2)). The resulting covers have diameters at most δ. Let the positive cost tolerance in F003 range arbitrarily close to zero. Then H^(q+1)_δ(F) is bounded by arbitrarily small positive costs, hence is zero. Every positive scale has zero content, so H^(q+1)(F)=0. Since q+1>0, E001 gives dim_H F≤q+1.

N001 gives 0<D≤n in the present branch, so D is a finite real number. The supremum of v+1 over real 0<v<D is D+1: for example the numbers D-D/k, indexed by integers k>1, lie in (0,D) and increase to D. F001 therefore gives dim_H F≥D+1. Discharge L1 to obtain precisely the asserted conditional lower bound.

patches.value: Choose x0∈E from H001. The map t↦(x0,t) from I into F preserves distances, because for t,u∈I, sqrt(dist(x0,x0)^2+|t-u|^2)=|t-u|. Here is the cover-based monotonicity argument for this particular isometric embedding, with all metric comparisons displayed. Fix real v,d and a sequence V, and temporarily assume L4: v>0, d>0 and V is a countable d-cover of F. Define T_i={t∈I:(x0,t)∈V_i}. These sets cover I; the distance identity gives diam(T_i)≤diam(V_i)≤d. Thus H^v_d(I)≤sum_i diam(V_i)^v. Discharge L4 and quantify v,d,V, retaining the positive exponent and scale and the cover conditions in the implication. Taking the infimum over such covers gives H^v_d(I)≤H^v_d(F) for every v>0,d>0. Taking suprema over d>0 gives H^v(I)≤H^v(F) for every v>0. By F004, H^v(F)=∞ for all 0<v<1. E001 gives dim_H F≥v for every such v, hence dim_H F≥1. Together with F004 these are the two exported dimension assertions. If D=0 the lower bound is dim_H F≥D+1. The same vertical-copy construction works for the unique point of Eucl(0); no positive ambient dimension was used.
A=F⊆Eucl(n+1), for every real exponent v∈(0,1); apply infinite measure⇒dimension≥v.
